emma: quick intake — customer (fintech) is asking for contract-backed reserved slots with a hard monthly cost cap + per-request latency SLO. we need to define acceptance criteria, rollout guardrails, and explicit fallback behavior when reserved capacity is saturated.

mike: want numbers: expected steady qps, burstiness, and percent of traffic that must hit reserved vs burst.

anya: customer estimate: 200 seats, ~0.8 req/min/seat, peak burst ~3x for 10m windows. will confirm tomorrow.

emma: goals i want captured in PRD:
- acceptance: p50/p95/p99 latency for typical prompt mix (p99 < 220ms target), throughput at commit capacity with <=5% tail errors.
- cost guardrail: monthly committed spend cap that must not be exceeded; if projected burn would breach cap, system triggers fallback policy.
- rollout: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% per-tenant with manual approval and eval hooks.

oliver: operational constraints: fallback must be observable and reversible; we need per-tenant metrics: fallback rate, error rate, token burn delta.

lee: security/compliance note: for this tenant some requests must stay in VPC/private deployment. fallback must respect data residency/KMS rules — no cross-tenant model spillover.

mike: engineering notes: two implementation options — (A) soft fallbacks within same deployment to a quantized variant; (B) route to hosted pool with CSP but isolate telemetry. option B may violate contract.

anya: customer preference is same compute footprint, they signed up for dedicated capacity. fallback to hosted is a last resort but they want explicit consent paths.

emma: non-goals: we will not build custom model re-training for this tenant as part of the initial launch. not addressing prompt-level per-user quota in phase 1.

oliver: acceptance criteria (draft):
- system maintains committed throughput for 95% of minutes in a billing month.
- p99 latency <= 220ms for canonical prompt set at commit capacity.
- fallback rate <= 2% after canary, with automated rollback if errors spike > 3x baseline.

mike: edge cases to call out:
- cold-starts when autoscaler spins GPUs up -> need cold-start SLA or warm pool.
- KV-cache invalidation when switching models during fallback.
- partial requests (streaming) mid-fallback.

emma: rollout plan bullets to put in PRD:
1) define canonical prompt set & synthetic traffic harness.
2) run perf validation on dedicated pool (QA).
3) canary to tenant shadow traffic (5%) for 48h, collect quality regressions.
4) gradual ramp (25% 24h -> 100% 72h) with manual gate.

anya: evaluation hooks: automatic quality checks (BLEU/embedding-similarity) and manual spot-checks. if quality drop > 5% vs baseline, halt rollout.

lee: compliance acceptance: KMS audit events available and egress checks in place before canary.

emma: questions for sales/legal to confirm: is hosted fallback acceptable with explicit customer opt-in? do contracts require on-prem only?

sarah: i can loop in legal tomorrow; sales said customer is flexible but wants documented fallbacks.

deploy-bot: scheduled: perf-harness-run at 2024-05-15T03:00Z (ci-3456)

mike: next steps for PRD: i'll draft a technical approach section with two fallback strategies + cost impact table. emma, can you add explicit success metrics and the canonical prompt set?

emma: yes — i'll push a starter prompt list and metrics today. tagging @sarah to track contract questions. :white_check_mark:
